Class ChromaticColors

java.lang.Object
net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.ChromaticColors
public class ChromaticColors extends Object
Provides source-compatible color registration and map views backed by shared definitions.

The public maps are views, not independent mutable stores. A write publishes through ChromaticDefinitions; a read observes a current immutable snapshot. Saving a map or its entry set does not freeze it. Each lookup and size query reads the current publication.

  • Each new iterator captures the entries from one snapshot. Returned entries keep their captured RGB values until their own setValue changes them. Later publications do not refresh the remaining entries. A saved entry set can report a new size while an older iterator still walks the earlier entries.
  • A successful entry.setValue(value) updates the entry and publishes its replacement. It fails with ConcurrentModificationException if the binding was removed or replaced in the meantime.
  • Iterator removal targets its last returned entry, including a successful setValue update through that entry. It leaves a replacement from another write in place.

Separate map operations can read different publications. Use ChromaticDefinitions.snapshot() when several lookup tables must come from one publication, or edit when related writes must publish together. Named writes retain the spelling described by NAMED_CUSTOM_FORMATTING.

    • CUSTOM_FORMATTING

      public static final Map<Character, Integer> CUSTOM_FORMATTING

    • NAMED_CUSTOM_FORMATTING

      public static final Map<String,Integer> NAMED_CUSTOM_FORMATTING
      Named-color view using the shared case policy and first-declaration precedence.

      Lookups follow the current case policy, but a write retains the supplied spelling. When matching ignores case, writing glow does not replace a declaration spelled Glow. Both remain registered, and the earlier spelling still wins lookup. Entries expose the normalized lookup key; their guarded setValue updates the original binding rather than choosing a new spelling.
